Place exploration, concept exploration, task practice, role-play, gaming, communication, slide show, building/scripting, instruction, machinima — non-mutually-exclusive, inductively coded from open-ended educator descriptions (FE, p.239-240).

11 activity categories x 5 benefit ratings; significant main effect for only 2 of 5 benefits (place/object familiarity; motivation/engagement), both driven by the 'instruction' category scoring higher; no significant effects for place exploration, task practice, role-play, or communication despite the authors' a priori hypothesized links (FE, p.242-243).

Dalgarno & Lee's own follow-up qualifies rather than confirms their 2009/2010 model: educators strongly endorsed all five benefits regardless of activity type, and the authors themselves propose this may reflect 'enthusiasm and positive attitude... more... than an evidence-based assessment' rather than genuine task-specific differentiation (FE, p.243-244) — a self-authored caution about their own theory's evidentiary strength.

Distinguished from 'learning benefit': what is 'afforded' is the task the technology is perceived as being useable for (after Norman 1999), not the outcome/benefit itself, treated as downstream of task performance (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.237).
